task.description:
RE-GATE of the ISS-0426 design after rework 1. You FAILED the prior revision on OQ-2. CODE-DESIGNER has revised the design in place (lib/letflow/design/iss426-wallclock-test-contention.md, commit 201cdf68). Your job is to decide PASS or FAIL on the REVISED design.

SCOPE OF THIS RE-GATE. You already verified and PASSED points 1, 4, 5 and 6 on the prior revision (seam soundness and the build_script_error/3 precedent; CI genuinely reaching mix letflow.check.test via ci.yml:126; AC4 compliance; the minimal/additive letflow.check.test.ex change). ORCH has independently re-confirmed the CI chain (.github/workflows/ci.yml:126 `mix letflow.check` -> mix.exs:91-108 alias list ending in `letflow.check.test`). Do not re-litigate those from scratch -- but DO confirm the rework did not disturb them, since the revision touched the scope header and sections 2.1, 3, 4 and 7, and now adds a SECOND seam to executor.ex.

THE THREE THINGS THAT MUST ACTUALLY CLEAR:

1. OQ-2's RESOLUTION -- the blocking item. New section 2.1.2 proposes a second @doc false test-only seam mirroring run_with_heap_limit/5's spawn/monitor/receive shape with the `after` clause REMOVED ENTIRELY (unbounded wait on the three remaining receive clauses). Verify against executor.ex:508-551 that this is mechanically sound, and specifically adjudicate CODE-DESIGNER's two load-bearing claims:
   (a) That removing the `after` clause PRESERVES the heap-kill mechanism, on the grounds that max_heap_size: %{kill: true} is enforced by the BEAM regardless of whether the caller is waiting. Confirm this is true, not merely plausible.
   (b) That it STRENGTHENS design section 5.3's ordering argument, because with no caller-issued Process.exit(pid, :kill) possible on this path, every :killed DOWN is unconditionally the BEAM's own heap enforcement and no timing-order disambiguation is needed. Check this does not quietly WEAKEN REQ-156's guarantee instead: read section 5.3 and satisfy yourself that the distinction it draws is genuinely made unnecessary rather than merely made unobservable.
   (c) THE DEADLOCK RISK, which the handoff raises as its own check and which the design must answer: an unbounded receive has NO timeout. Confirm the three remaining receive clauses are jointly EXHAUSTIVE over every way the spawned process can terminate -- normal reply, BEAM heap kill, and any other exit reason -- so a test using this seam cannot hang forever if the Lua VM neither replies nor dies. If a script can genuinely run unbounded (an infinite loop with no heap growth and no instruction budget), say what happens: does the instruction budget always bound it, or is a hang reachable? ExUnit's own per-test timeout is a backstop but a 60s hang is a materially worse failure mode than the flake being fixed, so if that is the outcome the design must say so and justify it.

2. THE RECONCILED COUNTS. CODE-DESIGNER now reports Group 1 = 14 call sites across 11 tests (11 nil-heap sites in 9 tests via 2.1.1, 3 heap-limited sites in 2 tests via 2.1.2) and Group 2 = 11 tagged tests (9 pure + 2 mixed), and states this matches your own independently-derived count exactly. Confirm the revised section 2.1 table's rows and its new Mechanism column are correct against the source file -- in particular that rows 605 and 644 are the ONLY heap-limited entries in that table, and that the parenthetical arithmetic (11 rows, 14 call sites, with 253/605/861 each contributing 2 calls) actually adds up.

3. THE MIXED TESTS (656, 887). The revision states their memory_result arms are mechanistically eligible for 2.1.2's seam, but deliberately leaves section 2.4's prior choice authoritative: tag-isolate the whole test rather than split mechanisms within one test body. Judge whether that is a defensible design decision or an inconsistency now that a mechanism for those arms demonstrably exists. Either verdict is acceptable if reasoned -- what you must not do is let it pass unexamined.

ALSO: the revision corrected a top-of-document scope header that had inaccurately claimed executor.ex was untouched. Confirm the header now accurately describes the TWO additive seams, and that section 3's four hard-constraint restatements are still true of the revised design (especially AC4 -- two new functions on a security-relevant module is more production surface than the prior revision proposed, so re-check that no EXISTING function's behavior changes and that run_with_heap_limit/5's own `after` clause survives byte-for-byte).

Read any file. Do not edit lib/ or test/. Complete the handoff with a clear PASS/FAIL and per-item verdicts; on PASS set next_action to route to ELIXIR-DEV, on FAIL back to CODE-DESIGNER. Commit to branch feature/WF03-ISS0426-20260902. This is rework 1 of max 3 -- a second FAIL leaves one attempt before ORCH must escalate, so make any FAIL precise and exhaustive: list everything that must change, not just the first thing you find.

result.summary:
RE-GATE HARD GATE: FAIL, on check 1(c) (deadlock-risk contract gap in the new section 2.1.2 heap-limited seam). Full revised design re-read (lib/letflow/design/iss426-wallclock-test-contention.md, commit 201cdf68, 684 diff lines), CODE-DESIGNER's rework1 handoff read in full, and the following re-verified directly against source rather than accepted from either agent: lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex:508-551 (run_with_heap_limit/5, byte-for-byte), executor.ex:40-90 (LUA-10 moduledoc restatement, the coordinator's cited lines confirmed accurate), executor.ex:400-427 (run_script/3, re-checked for a comparable argument), test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs lines 567-652 (the two REQ-156 workload scripts and both heap-limited call sites' max_instructions/max_heap_words literals), and git diff main...HEAD --stat (confirms executor.ex still has zero code changes on this branch -- design-only step, as expected).

PER-ITEM VERDICTS:

1(a) HEAP-KILL PRESERVED -- CONFIRMED TRUE, not merely plausible. max_heap_size: kill: true (executor.ex:517) is a spawn_opt enforced by the BEAM on the spawned process itself, independent of whether the parent is in a receive. Removing the caller's own after clause changes only what the caller waits for, never what the BEAM does to the child process. Design's claim holds without qualification.

1(b) ORDERING ARGUMENT STRENGTHENED, NOT MERELY OBSCURED -- CONFIRMED. The original argument in run_with_heap_limit/5 (killed observed before after could fire, so it is not the caller's kill) exists only because a caller-issued kill was POSSIBLE and needed disambiguating against the BEAM's own kill. With no after clause on this new seam, no caller-issued kill exists on this path at all -- there is nothing left to disambiguate against, so the REQ-156 distinction is not made unobservable, it is made structurally unnecessary. This is a real strengthening, verified against the actual receive-clause list, not an assertion.

1(c) DEADLOCK RISK -- FAIL, this is the blocking finding. Independently confirmed the general risk is real: executor.ex:54-62 (re-read directly, matches the coordinator's citation) states LUA-10's entire purpose is bounding a script that max_instructions CANNOT bound by construction -- an in-band, pcall-catchable counter that a script can trap and continue past via a goto-style escape (the exact pattern REQ-155 AC-2, executor_test.exs:389, uses and which is why layer 2/the wall-clock kill exists at all). The three remaining receive clauses in section 2.1.2's seam are exhaustive over every way the SPAWNED PROCESS can terminate, but that is not exhaustive over every way EXECUTION CAN END -- a workload that neither trips the heap limit nor ever returns leaves all three clauses permanently unmatched, and with no after clause the receive blocks forever, backstopped only by ExUnit's default 60s per-test timeout. That is a materially worse failure mode than the flake being fixed, exactly as flagged.

REACHABILITY AT THE SPECIFIC CALL SITES -- independently verified, matches the coordinator's own read: moderate_allocating_script (executor_test.exs:591-597, for i = 1, 20000 do ... end) and gigabyte_allocating_script (:568-577, for i = 1, 1000000 do ... end) are both fixed-iteration-count for-loops, run at both call sites (605, 644) under max_instructions: 1_000_000_000 -- no pcall-trap-and-continue construct at either site. Both workloads terminate via loop completion or heap kill, whichever comes first; the goto-escape pattern that motivates layer 2's existence at all is never used by anything section 2.1.2 currently covers. So the seam IS safe for the two call sites the design currently assigns it.

WHERE THE DESIGN FALLS SHORT -- the safety argument in section 2.1.2 (no Group-1 heap-limited test uses such a workload) is stated as an observation about CURRENT usage, never elevated into a stated CONTRACT on the seam itself. Compare with section 2.1.1's nil-heap seam: run_script/3 (executor.ex:400-427, re-checked) is ALWAYS bounded by Sandbox.new(max_instructions: budget) for any input except a goto-style construct -- a genuinely stronger, mechanism-level safety property that holds regardless of what future test authors pass in (modulo the same goto caveat, which no Group-1-assigned test uses). Section 2.1.2's safety is NOT a mechanism-level property -- it is a property of the two workloads currently assigned to it. The design never states this distinction, and never gives the new seam a binding usage contract (e.g. a @doc false comment stating callers MUST pass a workload that terminates independent of wall-clock enforcement -- a bounded loop, or a script that does not trap-and-continue past its own instruction budget via goto or similar). Without that contract, the seam is exactly the loaded-gun-for-the-next-caller risk the rework instruction's supplement described: safe today only because of what happens to be passed to it, not because the mechanism itself prevents an unsafe call. This must be fixed by stating an explicit, binding constraint on the seam's own contract (its @doc false declaration or equivalent design-level statement ELIXIR-DEV must carry into the docstring), not merely a per-call-site safety argument in prose.

2. RECONCILED COUNTS -- PASS, verified exactly. Section 2.1's revised table has 11 rows (test-declaration lines 253, 273, 283, 299, 448, 605, 644, 812, 861, 983, 1052), with 253 (AC-1, 2 calls), 605 (AC-1, 2 calls), and 861 (AC4, 2 calls) each contributing 2 timeout_ms call sites -- 11 + 3 = 14 call sites across 11 tests, matching my independently-derived count from the prior gate exactly. The Mechanism column correctly marks ONLY 605 and 644 as heap-limited -- independently confirmed by reading every max_heap_words value in the table's underlying call sites in the raw test file: 605 uses small_alloc_heap_words/a large literal (non-nil), 644 uses sixteen_mb_in_words (non-nil), every other row uses nil. Group 2 remains 11 tagged tests (9 pure + 2 mixed), unchanged from the already-correct prior revision. Arithmetic is sound throughout.

3. MIXED TESTS (656, 887) -- DEFENSIBLE, examined and reasoned, not rubber-stamped. Section 2.1.2 now provides a mechanism that COULD apply to the memory_result arms (mechanistically identical to 644's BEAM-heap-kill branch), but section 2.4 keeps tag-isolation authoritative for both tests. This is a sound call: (a) the whole test is already forced into Group 2's isolated partition regardless, because each test's OTHER arm (timeout_result) is a genuine, irreducible race that HARD CONSTRAINT 4 requires keeping -- so the memory_result arm inherits contention isolation for free the moment the test is tagged, independent of whether it also gets section 2.1.2's seam; (b) applying two different call mechanisms (one seamed, two literal) inside one three-call test body for no benefit visible from the test itself is a real, named readability cost the design correctly weighs against a benefit that does not materialize once (a) is true. This is not an oversight quietly left inconsistent with section 2.1's table -- section 2.1.2 explicitly says that choice, not this table, is authoritative for those two tests, which is the right way to flag a deliberate non-uniformity rather than let a reader infer an error. PASS on this item.

SCOPE HEADER AND HARD CONSTRAINTS RE-CHECK -- PASS. The header now accurately states two additive @doc false seams land in executor.ex (previously the prior revision inaccurately claimed executor.ex was untouched even though section 2.1.1 already put a seam there) -- this correction is confirmed accurate against section 2.1.1/2.1.2's actual content. Section 3's four hard-constraint restatements were re-checked: AC4 (point 1) now correctly enumerates run_with_heap_limit/5's own after clause as one of the byte-for-byte-unchanged items alongside execute_with_manifest/2,3 and handle_yield_result/3 -- verified true today by git diff main...HEAD --stat, which shows executor.ex absent from this branch's diff entirely (no code written yet, consistent with a design-only step); this is a requirement on ELIXIR-DEV's future implementation, correctly stated at design time, not yet falsifiable since no code exists. AC3/AC5/Group-2-detection-power (points 2-4) are unaffected by this rework, which touches only the heap-limited mechanism inside Group 1 -- confirmed by reading the diff of section 3 itself, no wording changed there beyond folding in the second seam's name.

POINTS 1/4/5/6 FROM THE PRIOR GATE -- spot-checked, not disturbed. The revision's changes are confined to the scope header and sections 2.1/2.1.1a/2.1.2/3/4/7; sections 2.2/2.3 (tag wiring) and section 6 are unchanged from the already-PASSED prior revision. Re-confirmed build_script_error/3's precedent (executor.ex:438-457) is still accurately cited in section 2.1.1a's comparison table. ORCH's independent re-confirmation of the CI chain (ci.yml:126 -> mix.exs:91-108 alias ending in letflow.check.test) is consistent with what I verified directly at the prior gate; nothing in this rework touches that wiring.

OVERALL: FAIL, on check 1(c) alone -- points 1(a), 1(b), 2, 3, and the scope/hard-constraint re-check all PASS. This is a narrower, more precise defect than the prior gate's: not a missing mechanism, but a missing CONTRACT on a mechanism that is correct for its current two call sites. Per this handoff's own instruction, this list is exhaustive -- nothing else in the revision needs to change.

issues.description: Check 1(c) -- section 2.1.2's new unbounded-wait seam has no stated usage contract, only a per-call-site safety argument. Independently confirmed the seam is safe for its two CURRENT call sites (605, 644: both fixed-iteration for-loops under a generous max_instructions, no pcall-trap-and-continue/goto construct), but the design's own safety reasoning (no Group-1 heap-limited test uses such a workload) is an observation about current usage, not a constraint on the mechanism -- unlike section 2.1.1's nil-heap seam, where run_script/3 is ALWAYS bounded by max_instructions regardless of input (modulo the same goto-escape caveat that motivates REQ-155 layer 2's own existence, which no Group-1-assigned test uses either way). A future test author adding a heap-limited Group-1-shaped test whose workload traps its own budget exhaustion and loops again (the exact pattern REQ-155 AC-2 uses, executor_test.exs:389) would silently inherit a seam that hangs forever, backstopped only by ExUnit's default 60s per-test timeout -- a materially worse failure mode than the flake ISS-0426 files. REQUIRED FIX: state an explicit, binding contract on the new seam -- in its @doc false declaration (carried forward into ELIXIR-DEV's implementation) or as an equally binding design-level statement -- along the lines of: callers MUST pass a workload that terminates independent of wall-clock enforcement (a bounded loop, or one that does not trap-and-continue past its own instruction budget via goto or an equivalent construct); this seam provides no bound of its own beyond the BEAM heap-kill. Section 2.1.2 should also explicitly note that this is why the two mixed tests' memory_result arms (656, 887) remain eligible in principle per its own text, since those workloads are the same bounded scripts -- the contract statement should make that eligibility judgment checkable by future readers, not only by this validator's own analysis this round.

result.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER: add an explicit, binding usage contract to section 2.1.2's new seam (and, for consistency, consider whether section 2.1.1's nil-heap seam should also state its own bound explicitly -- it already has one via max_instructions, but the design does not currently say so in contract terms) stating what workload shapes are safe to pass to the unbounded-wait seam and why (termination guaranteed by heap kill or natural completion, never by wall-clock patience). No other item in this re-gate requires a change -- checks 1(a), 1(b), 2, and 3 all PASS as reasoned in this handoff, and the scope header / hard-constraint restatements are accurate. Resubmit to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR.
